thought_process: Step 1: Analyzed the source text and identified the main ideas: what generative AI is, how language models work, how prompts and RAG help, and how AI agents use tools and work together.
Step 2: Grouped the content into six beginner-friendly lessons so that every major term and concept from the source is covered without adding outside information.
Step 3: Chose exactly three modules with two lessons each, ordered from core model ideas to prompting and then agents, to create a clear learning path for beginners.
title: Introduction to generative AI and agents

lessons.title: What generative AI is
lessons.slo: Describe generative AI as technology that can create human-like content using learned patterns, not magic.

lessons.title: Tokens, vectors, and embeddings
lessons.slo: Explain how text is split into tokens and turned into embeddings with help from a transformer.

lessons.title: How models predict the next word
lessons.slo: Explain how an LLM uses a prompt and context to predict the most likely next token.

lessons.title: Prompts, history, and RAG
lessons.slo: Identify system prompts, user prompts, conversation history, and retrieval augmented generation as ways to improve responses.

lessons.title: Building blocks of an AI agent
lessons.slo: Describe the three key parts of an AI agent: an LLM, instructions, and tools.

lessons.title: Multi-agent systems
lessons.slo: Explain how multiple agents can work together by sharing tasks through prompts.
